# DC Circuits

Ohm's law states that the current through a conductor is proportional to the voltage across it, as V = I × R, where R is the resistance in ohms.

Resistance is the opposition a material offers to the flow of electric current. Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance and is measured in siemens.

For resistors in series the total resistance is R = R1 + R2 + R3, and the same current flows through each resistor. For resistors in parallel the total resistance is given by 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2, and the same voltage appears across each resistor.

The power dissipated in a resistor is P = V × I = I^2 R watts.

Kirchhoff's current law states that the sum of currents entering a junction equals the sum of currents leaving it. Kirchhoff's voltage law states that the sum of voltages around any closed loop is zero.

Advantages of parallel connection
• Independence – each device works even if another fails.
• Same voltage – every device receives the full supply voltage.
